headline: President Bush updates Executive Order 12333, the main set of rules for how US intelligence agencies are organized and operate.
what_it_does: This order changes Executive Order 12333, a 1981 order that sets the basic rules for US intelligence work, including spying and information gathering. The title says it makes further amendments to those rules. No summary was provided, so the exact changes are not described here. The order was signed after Congress created the Director of National Intelligence in 2004, and updates around that time generally adjusted the rules to fit that new office.

who_it_affects.group: US intelligence agencies, such as the CIA, NSA, and FBI intelligence units
who_it_affects.how: The rules that guide their duties and activities are changed.
The order likely adjusts this official's role in leading the intelligence agencies, though the details are not given here.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed July 30, 2008; executive orders usually take effect when signed unless they say otherwise.
